title: 第0011章灶火重开第0012章骨火初燃
content_zh:
第0011章灶火重开清晨六点，阳光斜切过巷口，落在“刀鱼小灶”那块歪斜的招牌上。
店门敞着。
巴刀鱼蹲在门口刷台阶，动作缓慢，指节发白。他左臂缠着渗血的绷带，皮肤下仍有金火游走的痕迹，像未熄的炭。每动一下，命火便灼痛一分。
酸菜汤坐在门槛上，捧着一碗白粥，呼哧呼哧地喝。他身上多了几道新疤，眼神却比从前亮。
娃娃鱼靠在门框边，脸色仍有些苍白，可指尖已能稳稳夹住一片姜，轻轻含在唇间。她闭眼，像是在听什么。
“整条街的灶，都醒了。”她轻声道，“昨晚那场‘心火’，烧断了‘饲’的根。再没人会梦到吃汤了。”
巴刀鱼没说话，只是把最后一块地砖擦干净，站起身。
他推门进店。
店内已焕然一新。
灶台回来了。
不是原来的那个，而是从职工食堂带回的**第三口镇灶**。它被重新安在原位，锅底符文流转，银火在深处微微跳动，像一颗沉睡的心。
冰箱立着，里面塞满新鲜食材——酸菜汤昨晚翻墙从批发市场“借”来的，说是“他们欠的，该还了”。
案板、锅铲、调料架，全是他父亲用过的老物。他一件件擦过，摆好，动作轻得像在整理遗物。
“今天开张？”酸菜汤跟进来，拍了拍锅，“我饿了。”
“不开。”巴刀鱼摇头。
“不开？”娃娃鱼也进来，“为什么？”
“因为还没‘净’。”他走到灶前，掌心贴上锅壁，“这灶，曾被‘饲’污染。它压过‘井’，烧过‘尸’，也差点成了‘门’的钥匙。现在它回来了，可它的‘心’，还是黑的。”
他闭眼，命火缓缓注入。
银火自掌心流出，顺着符文蔓延，渗入锅体深处。
锅开始震。

不是轻颤，是剧震。
锅底，竟浮现出一张脸——灰白、扭曲，是那些被“饲”吞噬的亡魂。他们张嘴，无声嘶吼，怨气冲天。
“它在反抗。”娃娃鱼后退，“这口锅，吃过人。”
“那就清。”巴刀鱼咬牙，命火全开，“我不管它过去烧过什么。从今天起，它只准烧一样东西——”
他睁眼，声音如刀：
**“真味。”**
轰——！
银火炸开，化作光网，将整口锅笼罩！
锅中虚影疯狂挣扎，黑气翻腾，可银火如阳，寸寸焚之。
十分钟。
二十分钟。
巴刀鱼冷汗如雨，嘴角溢血，可手始终未离锅。
终于——
锅中一声轻响。
content_en:
Chapter 0011 The stove reopens. At six o'clock in the morning, the sun slants across the alley and falls on the crooked signboard of "Swordfish Xiaozao".
The store door is open.
The bass fish squatted at the door and scrubbed the steps, his movements were slow and his knuckles were white. His left arm was wrapped in a bleeding bandage, and there were still traces of golden fire swimming under his skin, like unquenched coals. Every time he moved, the life fire burned a little bit.
Pickled cabbage soup was sitting on the threshold, holding a bowl of white porridge and drinking it. He had a few new scars on his body, but his eyes were brighter than before.
The baby fish was leaning against the door frame, her face still a little pale, but she could already hold a piece of ginger firmly between her fingertips and hold it gently between her lips. She closed her eyes as if listening to something.
"Everyone in the street is awake." She said softly, "The 'heart fire' last night burned out the roots of 'feeding'. No one will dream of eating soup anymore."
The bass fish didn't say anything, just wiped the last floor tile clean and stood up.
He opened the door and entered the store.
The store has been given a new look.
The stove is back.
Not the original one, but the **Third Stove Suppressor** brought back from the staff canteen. It was placed back in place, the runes on the bottom of the pot flowed, and the silver fire beat slightly in the depths, like a sleeping heart.
The refrigerator was standing, filled with fresh ingredients - the pickled cabbage soup was "borrowed" from the wholesale market over the wall last night, saying that "they owe it, and it's time to pay it back."
The chopping board, spatula, and spice rack are all old items used by his father. He wiped them one by one and arranged them, his movements as light as arranging relics.
"Opening today?" Sauerkraut Soup followed and patted the pot, "I'm hungry."
"Don't open it." Basio fish shook his head.
"Not open?" Baby Fish also came in, "Why?"
"Because it's not 'clean' yet." He walked to the stove and put his palm against the wall of the pot. "This stove was once polluted by 'feeding'. It crushed the 'well', burned the 'corpse', and almost became the key to the 'door'. Now it is back, but its 'heart' is still black."
He closed his eyes, and the life fire slowly poured into him.
The silver fire flowed out from the palm, spread along the runes, and penetrated deep into the pot.
The pot started to shake.
Not a slight tremor, but a severe tremor.
A face appeared at the bottom of the pot - gray and twisted, it was the souls of those devoured by "Feed". They opened their mouths and roared silently, filled with resentment.
"It's resisting." The giant salamander backed away, "This pot has eaten people."
"Then clean it up." The swordfish gritted its teeth, and its life was fully activated. "I don't care what it burned in the past. From today on, it can only burn one thing -"
He opened his eyes and his voice was like a knife:
**"Real flavor."**
Boom——!
The silver fire exploded and turned into a network of light, covering the entire pot!
The phantom in the pot struggled wildly, and black energy surged, but the silver fire was like the sun, burning every inch.
Ten minutes.
Twenty minutes.
The fish was sweating like rain, and blood was bleeding from the corners of its mouth, but its hands never left the pot.
Finally——
There was a soft sound in the pot.
